title: SLA-aware georouter with decaying anomaly weights and fallback model selector
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem: Region selection currently uses raw percentile thresholds that react abruptly to transient spikes and do not account for customer-level SLOs or short-lived network anomalies. We need a georouting policy that (1) combines p50/p95 latency with network health signals (packet loss, tcp retransmits, error rates) into a single composite score, (2) applies decaying anomaly weights so isolated spikes don't cause immediate global failovers, and (3) ties selection to per-customer SLA tiers while gracefully falling back to compatible model variants (quantized/smaller) when capacity or latency SLOs are at risk.

Proposal: Implement an SLA-aware georouter that computes per-region composite scores using an exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) over multiple telemetry channels (p50, p95, packet_loss_pct, tcp_err_rate). Anomaly events (deviations beyond baseline stdev) are tracked as short-lived signals with a configurable decay half-life; multiple repeated anomalies escalate region penalty faster. The composite score is adjusted by customer tier (gold/silver/free) so higher-tier customers bias selection toward lower-latency regions. When the top-ranked region is unhealthy or would violate the SLA for a request, route to the next-ranked region or to a local fallback model variant pre-registered for that region (e.g., quantized-8bit, small-llm) depending on latency/cost tradeoffs.

Key algorithmic points: compute baseline distributions per-region and per-model variant; use EWMA with alpha derived from target SLO window; compute anomaly_score = max(0, (observed - baseline_mean)/baseline_std) and multiply by anomaly_weight that decays exponentially over time; final region_penalty = weighted_sum(EWMA_p50, EWMA_p95*1.5, anomaly_score*2, packet_loss*3) normalized to 0-100. Incorporate hysteresis by requiring persistent penalty delta > threshold for N intervals before evicting region for routing.

Why different: This emphasizes decaying anomaly weighting (soft, time-decayed penalties) and explicit SLA-aware routing coupled with automated, model-variant fallbacks. It aims to avoid brittle flip-flopping while keeping deterministic, auditable decisions for post-incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Composite region score emits as a single metric per-region (region.composite_score) with p50/p95 and health components visible in Console
Routing policy respects customer tier: gold traffic should not be routed to higher-latency regions if a gold-compliant path exists
Transient single-interval spikes do not trigger failover; only sustained anomalies (configurable) increase region penalty enough to cause reroute
Fallback flow routes to configured model variant when top region would violate SLA, and the fallback is tracked in traces and billing
End-to-end tests simulate latency spike and packet loss and show correct decay behavior and safe rollback to original region after recovery
Dashboard and alerting show root-cause signals and a changelog of region decisions for at least 30 days
design_notes: Telemetry inputs: p50_ms, p95_ms, packet_loss_pct, tcp_err_rate, infra_error_rate. Each input is ingested as a time-series with windowed EWMAs.
Decay model: anomaly_weight(t) = base_weight * exp(-ln(2) * t / half_life_seconds). Default half_life_seconds = 300s (5m).
SLA tiers: gold/silver/free; map tiers to maximum acceptable composite_score thresholds and preferred regions list.
Fallback mapping: region -> ordered list of compatible model variants. Variants annotated with expected latency percentiles and quality loss estimations.
Hysteresis: require penalty_delta > X for M consecutive windows before making changes; X and M configurable per-customer tier.
Observability: instrument events: routing_decision, region_penalty_breakdown, anomaly_event_start/stop, fallback_activation.
Privacy/security: no customer prompt payloads are used in scoring; only telemetry and metadata. Audit logs preserved in Private deployments per retention policy.
tasks: 1) Implement composite scoring library (Rust) with EWMA and decaying anomaly weight logic
2) Expose new metrics in runtime telemetry pipeline and update metrics schema (region.composite_score + breakdown tags)
3) Add SLA tier lookup and enforcement in routing decision path
4) Implement fallback model variant selector and safe invocation path with tracing
5) End-to-end test harness: synthetic latency/packet loss generator and verification scripts
6) Console dashboard: per-region score panel + time-travel debug + routing decisions log
7) Run gradual rollout: internal canary -> progressive percent rollout -> global by region
8) Post-deploy: run 72-hour soak, review metrics, and iterate on half_life and hysteresis params
